about.title: Seaside Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A defective product doesn't announce itself before it hurts someone — it might be a car part that fails on Fremont Boulevard, a faulty appliance in a Broadway Avenue apartment, or a tool that malfunctions on a job site near Del Monte Boulevard. California generally applies strict liability to these cases, meaning an injured Seaside resident usually doesn't have to prove a manufacturer was careless — only that the product was defective and that the defect caused harm. That single legal difference can matter a great deal for families in Monterey County trying to understand their options after an injury. LawProactive doesn't practice law or represent claimants directly; instead, we connect people in Seaside with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate the product, the defect, and who along the supply chain — manufacturer, distributor, or retailer — may share responsibility. There's no cost to get connected, and no fee owed unless the attorney recovers on your behalf.

whyChoose.title: Why Strict Liability Matters for Seaside Claimants

items.title: No Need to Prove Negligence
items.desc: Because California often applies strict liability to defective products, an injured person generally must show the defect and the harm it caused, not that the manufacturer was careless.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which may widen the pool of parties an attorney can pursue on a claimant's behalf.

items.title: Preserving the Product Preserves the Case
items.desc: Keeping the defective item intact and unaltered after an injury is often critical, since it may serve as the central evidence in a design, manufacturing, or warning-defect claim.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer knew about the defect?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California's strict liability approach generally focuses on whether the product itself was defective and caused injury, rather than what the manufacturer knew or intended. An independent attorney can review the specifics of your situation to explain how this applies.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, without repairs or alterations, and store it somewhere safe. This physical evidence often plays a major role in showing a design, manufacturing, or warning defect. An attorney can advise on proper handling and documentation.

items.question: Does it matter that I live in Seaside specifically?
items.answer: Your claim would generally be handled under California law regardless of city, but local details — like where the product was purchased or used, whether near Del Monte Boulevard or Noche Buena Street — can help an attorney piece together the timeline. Monterey County court procedures may also come into play depending on where a case is filed.

items.question: Is there any cost to get connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive's connection service is free, and the independent attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation.
